summary: Radar for 2026-10-19 (GLP-1 focus). The biggest story today is gray-market and authenticity news, which is our strongest lane on YouTube. STAT and MDLinx report the FDA received two death reports (July and September) after people used products sold as retatrutide. The FDA would not say whether it verified them, and Lilly says neither person was in a trial. Futurism, NL Times and Stocktwits picked this up Oct 17–19, alongside Lilly's six lawsuits. Separately, USA Today and AOL (Oct 19) and Medical Daily report a Class II recall of compounded tirzepatide/niacinamide vials from Houston RX: 64 vials, started Sep 25, after an FDA inspection logged 14 observations. LA Times (Oct 19) also re-ran the Bloomberg story about black mold at Chinese plants making compounded ingredients. Fresh science hooks: SciTechDaily (Oct 19) brought TRANSCEND-T2D-1 to a general audience (retatrutide in type 2 diabetes, 40 weeks, Lancet), which feeds a 'Did retatrutide beat tirzepatide?' decoder. That decoder must say there is no head-to-head trial and that Lilly plans to file in Q1 2027, which is not approval. Other hooks: commentary on orforglipron's ACHIEVE-4 heart-safety trial vs insulin glargine, and a large matched cohort in Age and Ageing on GLP-1s and fatty liver in adults 65 and over (observational, 43,930 per group). Head-to-head and evergreen tirzepatide body-effect questions stay the reliable backbone for both YouTube and Instagram. Seasonal: Halloween and Thanksgiving eating questions are about to start. Rejected: how-to advice on switching from compounded semaglutide.

candidates.topic: Black-market 'retatrutide': what's confirmed about the FDA death reports and Lilly's lawsuits (as of Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: A calm 'what's confirmed?' Short. Retatrutide is investigational and not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026. Lilly says it plans to file in Q1 2027, and a plan to file isn't approval. STAT reports the FDA received two death reports after use of products sold as retatrutide (July and September). The FDA would not say whether it verified them, and Lilly says neither person was in a trial. Lilly has filed six lawsuits against sellers, and its CMO says the black-market product is 'not a medicine'. Attribute every line to the FDA, Lilly or STAT and never name sellers. Close by pointing to a prescriber about approved options or clinical trials. YouTube only.
candidates.why_now: Futurism (Oct 17), NL Times (Oct 19, rising illegal use in the Netherlands) and Stocktwits are amplifying the death reports and lawsuits, and autocomplete-style 'retatrutide approval status' queries fill today's news feed. Our Reddit retatrutide Short is at 116 views and climbing, our best lane.

candidates.topic: Did retatrutide beat tirzepatide? What the type 2 diabetes trials show (TRANSCEND-T2D-1 and TRIUMPH-2), with no head-to-head trial yet
candidates.angle: A long-form decoder in our only breakout format. In TRANSCEND-T2D-1 (537 adults with type 2 diabetes managed with diet and exercise, 40 weeks, Lancet), retatrutide was compared with placebo. Average weight loss was about 11.5–15.3% across the dose arms vs 2.6% on placebo, and A1C fell up to 1.94 points on 12 mg vs 0.81 on placebo. Set this beside the published tirzepatide SURPASS trials as a cross-trial comparison, labelled 'not head-to-head'. Status: investigational, and Lilly plans to file in Q1 2027, which isn't approval. Mention the common stomach side effects briefly. A Short version could lead with 'Retatrutide in type 2 diabetes: how much weight?'
candidates.why_now: SciTechDaily's 'New triple-action drug helps people with diabetes lose up to 15%' (Oct 19) is moving the trial from journals into general news, and retatrutide searches are already up because of the black-market story. EloraTZP's decoder got 407 views.

evidence.signal: Results of the first Phase 3 retatrutide study in type 2 diabetes (TRANSCEND-T2D-1)

candidates.topic: Is the orforglipron pill safe for the heart? ACHIEVE-4: orforglipron vs insulin glargine in type 2 diabetes (Lancet, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Frame it as a safety question that names both drugs. ACHIEVE-4 enrolled more than 2,700 adults with type 2 diabetes at higher heart risk. MACE-4 was 16% lower relative to insulin glargine (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.59–1.20), which met non-inferiority: 'as safe as', not proven better. The lower death rates were pre-planned analyses, not the main result. The Clinical Trial Vanguard (Oct 19) says it 'raised the bar' for other oral GLP-1s. Give a dated status: FDA-approved as Foundayo in the US, and in the EU the CHMP recommended it on Oct 16 with the Commission decision pending.
candidates.why_now: A fresh trade-press angle (Oct 19) on top of five snapshots of orforglipron EU momentum. A safety head-to-head that names both drugs fits our Instagram winners. Orforglipron alone underperforms as a Short, so name both drugs and keep the long-form for later.

evidence.signal: ACHIEVE-4: MACE-4 HR 0.84 (0.59–1.20) vs insulin glargine, non-inferiority met; Lancet publication
